_source: The Western Front Companion pp. 202-221 and Middlebrook appendices; mine count and Y Sap time from web sources (Wikipedia 'Mines on the first day of the Somme'). Times are 1 July 1916 unless stated.

mines.name: Hawthorn Ridge Redoubt
mines.effect: Blown ten minutes early; warned the Germans (RIR 119); crater 130 ft across and 58 ft deep; Germans occupied the rim

mines.name: Y Sap
mines.sector: III Corps, 34th Division, north of La Boisselle

mines.name: Lochnagar
mines.sector: III Corps, 34th Division, south of La Boisselle (Schwaben Höhe)

mines.name: Kasino Point
mines.effect: Fired after the infantry had left their trench; debris fell on the advancing men; destroyed the machine-gun post

minesTotal: 19 mines (8 large, 11 small) on the British front; the 11 small ones further south are not yet located

timeline.event: B and D Companies, 1st Lancashire Fusiliers, with four Stokes mortars, move by tunnel into the Sunken Lane in no man's land
Final intense bombardment begins
Hurricane bombardment of the German positions; the German headquarters in Glatz Redoubt already destroyed by howitzer fire
Germans shell the Sunken Lane and the British front line; the British bombardment is at its heaviest
109th Brigade (36th Division) leaves its trenches and creeps forward (15 min before the lift)
Russian saps, tunnelled under no man's land to within 20 yards of the German front, are blown open; trench mortars open fire
Hawthorn Ridge mine; VIII Corps heavy artillery lifts off the German front line
Smoke screen laid; 56th Division leading companies move into no man's land
Two platoons of 2nd Royal Fusiliers with four machine guns and four Stokes mortars rush the Hawthorn crater; hurricane mortar bombardment from the Sunken Lane
Stokes mortar hurricane bombardment
17th HLI creep forward towards the Leipzig Salient
9th Company, Reserve Infantry Regiment 119, counter-attacks at the new Hawthorn crater
Smoke screen on the inner flanks of the two attacking divisions
Lochnagar, Y Sap and Tambour mines
Zero hour
1st Lancashire Fusiliers attack from the Sunken Lane and are cut down; only about 50 reach the dip in no man's land. 1st East Lancashires and 1st Hampshires find the wire largely uncut
2nd South Wales Borderers head for Y Ravine; few get within 100 yards of the German front line
Captain Nevill, 8th East Surreys, kicks off his company's advance with one of four footballs; a Livens flame projector clears the western edge of the Crater Field
Colonel Fairfax of the 17th King's goes forward arm in arm with Commandant Le Petit of the French 153rd Infantry Regiment
2nd Seaforth Highlanders and 2nd Royal Dublin Fusiliers halted by machine guns in no man's land
1st South Staffords in Cemetery Trench, outskirts of Mametz
16th Middlesex attack; fewer than 120 men reach the Hawthorn crater
1st Border Regiment attacks from the second-line trenches and suffers the same fate; C Company, 1st Lancashire Fusiliers, loses all but 50 men trying to reach the Sunken Lane
46th Division fourth wave goes over as the smoke clears; checked by machine guns
Schwaben Redoubt taken by 36th Division; 11th Border (32nd Division) caught moving up
90th Brigade (30th Division) begins the advance on Montauban
Advancing troops reach and capture Glatz Redoubt
14th Brigade (1st Dorsets) advances on the Leipzig Redoubt
107th Brigade moves towards the German second line
1st Newfoundland Regiment attacks from the third line and loses 710 men; few reach no man's land
29th Division attack has failed; 4th Division's 10th Brigade advance goes ahead though a halt order was sent
Pommiers Redoubt captured by the 18th Division after a fierce fight

Leipzig Salient: German reserves (13th Company and the recruit company of R.I.R. 99, and 3rd Company of Bavarian R.I.R. 8) come up through the Hindenburg and Hohenzollern trenches and hold the 32nd Division at the Granatloch (time approximate)
timeline.source: German regimental maps reproduced in the owner's research

timeline.event: 107th Brigade within 100 yards of the Grandcourt line and Stuff Redoubt, caught by its own barrage
British troops enter the western end of Train Alley
Under fierce counter-attack and short of ammunition, resistance in the Hawthorn crater collapses (about 10:30); survivors return to the British lines
Montauban village captured by the 30th Division
Montauban Alley reached north of the village; 16th Manchesters capture field guns of German Field Artillery Regiment 21
20th King's capture the Briqueterie (brickworks) after a bombardment
50th Brigade (7th East Yorks, 7th Green Howards) attacks Fricourt after a weak bombardment; fails
7th Division's final effort; Mametz secured
18th Division reaches White Trench

Afternoon: German counter-attacks close on the Schwaben Redoubt from three sides: Gruppe Prager from Grandcourt, Gruppe Beyerköhler (later Wurm) and companies of Bavarian R.I.R. 8 from Feste Staufen, Abteilung Lunau (14th Company, R.I.R. 99) along the Auwärter-Weg (time approximate)
timeline.source: German regimental maps reproduced in the owner's research

timeline.event: 21st Division ordered to consolidate
7th Division reaches Bunny Alley-Fritz Trench (map notes say about 19:00)
With Montauban and Pommiers Redoubt taken, German resistance in the centre collapses; all of Montauban Alley in British hands
Evening: poorly co-ordinated German counter-attacks on Montauban are driven off
Heavier German counter-attacks force the 36th Division back from the Schwaben Redoubt
Only about 750 yards of the German front line still held by the 36th Division
Last company (1st Royal Irish Fusiliers) leaves the Quadrilateral
